documents.title: Doc 75 - DECISION - Car 24 - Alleged unsafe release
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 24 - Alleged unsafe release

details.fact: During the feature race Car 24 was released from its pit box ahead of Car 22.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 28.12 (a) of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 58 and 59) and heard the Driver and team representative of Car 3 and Car 12 and reviewed video evidence. The driver of car 24 reported that he left his pit position as soon as he was signaled to do so. He said he saw that there were no cars in the fast lane behind. He said that he had some wheel spin from the wet conditions but upon entering the fast lane he saw that car 22 was now fully in the fast lane, and decided that it was safer to continue than to brake. The driver of car 22 reported that he saw car 24 entering ahead and had to lift and tap his brakes a little. The stewards considered the evidence and determined that the fast lane was indeed still empty when car 24 was released, car 22 having been released only a moment before and still accelerating to the pit lane speed as car 24 entered. Although the cars ended up in close proximity, it did not reach the threshold of being unsafe in the conditions and under these particular circumstances. It appeared that both drivers acted appropriately and no rule was breached.

documents.title: Doc 74 - DECISION - Car 3 - Alleged unsafe release
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 3 - Alleged unsafe release

details.fact: Car 3 (Miyata) was allegedly released unsafely from pit stop into the path of Car 12 (Boya).
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 28.12 (a) of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 56 and 57) and heard the Driver and team representative of Car 3 and Car 12 and reviewed video evidence. The driver of Car 3 reported that he left his pit position as soon as he was signaled to do so. He said he had some wheel spin from the wet conditions but thought he was only slightly delayed. The driver of Car 12 reported that he saw Car 3 being released and had to lift and brake in order not to have a collision. He felt that the release by the team of car 3 created an unsafe situation. The stewards considered the evidence and concluded that the situation was very close to being unsafe but it did not reach the threshold in the conditions and under these particular circumstances. It appeared that both drivers acted appropriately and no rule was breached.

documents.title: Doc 71 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 16 - Safety car infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 16 - Safety car infringement

details.fact: Crossed the white line at pit entry.
details.infringement: Breach of ISC Apdx L Chap IV (d)
details.decision: Warning to driver
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 54). At the start of the race Lap 1 Turn 1 an incident occurred necessitating the deployment of the Safety Car. As the leaders were approaching T17 the Race Director notified the teams that the drivers should follow Safety Car through the pit lane. Panels 19 and 20 were illuminated with a yellow arrow pointing to the right. The RD used this signal per Art 40.11 with the intention of notifying the drivers to enter the pit lane. The leader was approximately 50 meters before panel 19 when it was illuminated. The track condition was very wet and there was significant spray reducing visibility although it appeared from the drivers onboard camera that the panels were visible. There is no way for the Stewards to know when the drivers were notified by radio of the RD’s instruction to enter the pit lane. Some teams may react quicker than others and it is impossible to know what other radio traffic may affect how quickly the message can be delivered to individual drivers. The light panel signal showing a red arrow on a yellow background is used to indicate to a driver the side of the track that they should chose because of an issue in the area. It is not an exclusive instruction to enter the pit lane. The RD Competition Notes does not specifically state that when panels 19 and 20 are illuminated in this way that drivers are to enter the pit lane. Car 16 (Maini) entered the pit entry road and then returned to the track after the bollard at SC1 in breach of ISC Apex L Ch IV (d) and in contravention to the Race Directors instructions. The driver explained that he did not have clear radio communication from his engineer until very late and it was to “follow safety car through pit lane”. He did not see a Safety Car. He understood that the arrow signal on light panel 20 meant that he was to stay to that side of the track and take an alternate route. Having no clear instruction on what to do and then seeing drivers behind him staying out on track he chose to return to the track after the bollard. While the driver failed to follow the intended instructions from the Race Director no driver benefited nor was harmed. When racing was resumed after the safety car period all drivers were in the correct positions with no advantage gained. Consequently the Stewards decide that while the regulations were breached the appropriate penalty in this case is a Warning to the driver given the late call and the lack of clarity surrounding the instructions.

documents.title: Doc 67 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 22 - Causing a collsion

documents.title: Doc 65 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 17 - Failing to serve time penalty correctly
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 17 - Failing to serve time penalty correctly

details.fact: Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) failed to serve the ten-second (10) time penalty (Document 64) correctly.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 39.4 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Drive through penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (c.) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence and reviewed timing. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that having been previously issued a ten-second time penalty for causing a collision, Car 17 made a pit stop and failed to serve the referred penalty correctly. In the light of the present case, the Stewards elected to impose the Drive Through for failing to serve correctly the time penalty imposed.

documents.title: Doc 64 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 17 - Causing a collision
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 17 - Causing a collision

details.fact: Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) collided with Car 6 in Turn 1
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2 penalty points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 2 penalty points.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed video evidence. On the first lap Car 17 attempted an inside pass on Car 6 in the braking zone to Turn 1 and collided prior to the apex, with the left front of Car 17 making contact with the right rear of Car 6. It is clearly evident that Car 17 never achieved a substantial overlap on Car 6, Car 17's front axle only coming forward of Car 6's rear axle immediately prior to the collision. Although the incident occurred on the first lap, the Stewards do not find any pressure on either car that would mitigate the incident. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that the Driver of Car 17 was wholly to blame for the collision and impose a 10 second penalty on Car 17 accordingly.

documents.title: Doc 44 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 16 - Pit lane infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 16 - Pit lane infringement

details.fact: Team personnel from Car 16 worked on the car in the fast lane at pit exit
details.infringement: Breach of Article 28.4 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A fine of 500 Euros to be paid by the Team. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 42). Car 16 Maini stalled on the formation lap and was pushed by marshals to the pit lane. Team personnel retrieved the car and started it again. However, they sent the car to the pit exit too early and it had to sit for an extended period and the driver had to shut off the engine to avoid an overheating situation. Team personnel then started the car while it was in the fast lane at the pit exit. There were no other cars in the pit lane at the time and the driver gained no sporting advantage by this team error. Consequently the stewards determine that a team fine is appropriate.

documents.title: Doc 43 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - Gaining lasting advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - Gaining lasting advantage

details.fact: Car 20 (Fittipaldi) went off track while completing a pass on Car 4 (Herta) at Turns 11-12 thereby gaining lasting advantage.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 12.4.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. Approaching Turn 11 Car 20 attempted an outside pass on Car 4, then went off track and rejoined at Turn 12 completing an overtake over Car 4. To have the rights for a turn the car who is trying to overtake on the outside has to have its front axle ahead of the front axle of the other car at the apex, and in this case Car 20 was not in this position. The Stewards considered that Car 20 went off track at the exit of Turn 11 and rejoined at Turn 12 gaining a position over Car 4. A successful overtake requires the driver to complete the manoeuvre on track. Having analysed extensively the matter, the Stewards, under these circumstances considered that failing to lose an advantage constitutes gaining an advantage. The stewards elect to impose the standard penalty for leaving the track and gaining a lasting advantage.

details.decision: A fine of €500 to be paid by the Team. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the FIA International Sporting Code, fines shall be paid within forty-eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards examined photographic evidence. They summoned and heard the team representative (document 16). The team representative accepted the fact that the team member wearing shorts. Stewards determined that a team member of Car 20 working near the car was not wearing long trousers during the session, therefore decided to fine the team with 500 Euros.

documents.title: Doc 26 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - Failure to follow RD instructions - chequered flag
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - Failure to follow RD instructions - chequered flag

details.fact: Car 20 (Fittipaldi) failed to follow the Race Director Competition Notes (document 4) instructions for returning to the Support Paddock pit lane after the end of the session.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code - in conjunction with Item 25.1 of the Race Director’s Competition Notes.
details.decision: Warning
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 15). The drivers were informed by the FIA Race Director during the Drivers Meeting that after taking the chequered flag they must continue and leave the track via the exit after Turn 10, to the F2 Paddock Parc Fermé. Car 9 was the first car to receive the chequered flag in the Practice session closely followed by Car 20. It is noteworthy that the last car not to have received the chequered flag was just in front of Cars 9 and 20. The Driver reported that he did not see the chequered flag at the line nor any yellow flag / light panel nor marshals on track signalling for him to turn into the support paddock, as they had expected. As a result he did not exit after Turn 10 and he continued on the track in breach of the RD instructions. The Stewards considered the mitigating circumstances that no yellow flag was shown nor light panel was illuminated and the facts of the configuration of this new circuit and the short time between the last car that had not seen the chequered flag and the first car that crossed the line after the session finished was very short and as such the marshals could not be on track and waving the flag. However, it is responsibility of the driver to follow the RD instructions and he did not. Therefore, in the light of the present case and given the mitigating circumstances mentioned above, the Stewards elect to give a warning to the driver.

documents.title: Doc 24 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 1 - Failure to follow RD instructions
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 1 - Failure to follow RD instructions

details.fact: Car 1 (Rafael Camara) conducted a practice start from outside the marked grid boxes.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code in conjunction with Item 16.1 of the Race Director’s Competition Notes.
details.decision: Reprimand (non driving) given to the Driver of Car 1. This is his first Reprimand of the 2026 Season.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (documents 13). In a queue departing Pit Lane at the resumption of the session, Car #1 moved to the right side of the Pit Exit and slowed but came to a stop forward of both marked "grid boxes" on the right-hand side of the Pit Exit, and conducted a practice start. The driver of #1 explained that he intended to conduct a practice start but admitted that he had missed the location of the first markings because he was looking down while adjusting their settings. Noting that the driver did leave adequate room for other cars to pass, the Stewards accept the driver’s prompt admission of an error but nonetheless find that this was failure to follow the Race Director’s instructions for conducting practice starts and warrants the imposition of a Reprimand as the appropriate penalty.

documents.title: Doc 23 - DECISION - Car 10 - Alleged yellow flag infringement
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 10 - Alleged yellow flag infringement

details.fact: Car 10, Oliver Goethe, was alleged to have failed to comply with the double waving yellow flag requirements.at Turns11 and 12 during the practice session.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence and GPS evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representative (document 12). A yellow flag was shown at the entrance to turn 11 and then a double yellow entering turn 12 where there was a stopped car on the outside of the track on the exit. The driver of Car 10 reported that he was aware of both the yellow flag and the double yellow flag and he thought that he had lifted sufficiently. The mini sector data was reviewed with the driver and after analysis it was determined that the driver had slowed significantly in both mini sectors. As a result the Stewards find that the driver acted appropriately and no rule was breached and therefore take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 22 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Yellow flag infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Yellow flag infringement

details.fact: Car 23, Rafael Villagomez, did not comply with the requirement to reduce speed under single and double yellow flags at Turns 11 and 12 during the practice session.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A drop of 10 places on the grid for the Sprint and Feature races in which the driver participates. In addition, 3 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 3 points.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence and GPS evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representative (document 11). A yellow flag was shown at the entrance to turn 11 and then a double yellow entering turn 12 where there was a stopped car on the outside of the track on the exit. The driver of Car 23 reported that he was aware of both the yellow flag and the double yellow flag and he thought that he had lifted sufficiently. He then reported that after seeing that he was clear of the stopped car he resumed his push lap. The mini sector timing data revealed that the driver achieved his fastest time in both mini sectors up to that point in the session. There was no indication that the driver had lifted nor that he had abandoned his lap as is required when passing through a double yellow flag area. This is a violation of the regulations and relates to safety. The standard penalty of 10 grid drops is used as the Stewards could find no mitigating circumstances to vary the penalty. In keeping with Art 31.5 of the 2026 F2 Sporting Regulations the grid drop penalty will be applied to both the Sprint and Feature races.
